Incoming Apple CEO John Ternus is reportedly planning a "wholesale revamp" of Apple, attempting to make the company "faster and leaner," according to a new report from Bloomberg. The overhaul includes shipping more products, cutting "middle management roles," and several other changes.

John Ternus wants to reshape Apple — here's what he's envisioning

First, the incoming Apple CEO wants to ship more products faster than before, including being "more experimental." One idea is breaking Apple's longtime rhythm of "first half of the year and second half of the year" releases, in favor of a more even cadence throughout the year.

Ternus also wants to "create a leaner, more engineering-focused organization," with several cost-cutting and restructuring measures. One change is "removing some middle-management positions to shorten the chain between engineers and executives."

The report says Apple has already laid off "a group of engineering project managers (EPMs)" in the hardware engineering division over the past two weeks. Bloomberg described the roles as "central to Apple's product development process for decades," responsible for "managing timelines and coordinating work between teams."

The report noted: "Those affected included several project managers, around six of whom were directors — one of the most senior employee ranks at the company." "These employees were given just weeks to find other positions within the company; those who can't find a new role will be let go later this year."

However, Bloomberg says the cost-cutting measures may go even further. Ternus reportedly argued years ago that Apple should be "leaner":

Additionally, Apple reportedly shelved a plan this summer to cut 5,000 AppleCare employees, deciding that AI agents could take over the work.

Meanwhile, Ternus wants to grow Apple services revenue alongside Eddy Cue and CFO Kevan Parekh. The report says: "They've discussed launching new services, as well as extracting more revenue from existing products and services."
